newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Poland 97 inflation aim difficult - c. bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Poland 97 inflation aim difficult - c. bank chief.

text.p: Polish central bank chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said on Wednesday the government's 13-percent inflation goal for 1997 would be difficult to achieve and warned that unrealistic targets could endanger the bank's credibility.
"We'd like to be as close as possible to 13 percent, but it will be very difficult," she told reporters during an economic conference in Vienna.
"We can't honestly say to the people that inflation will indeed fall to 13 percent without risking our credibility," she added.
The government has said it expects inflation to drop to 13 percent by the end of the year, from 17 percent at the end of 1996, and to ease to single digits in less than two years.
"We have to fight against inflation. Our credibility is very important," the central bank chief said.

She also said the central bank's influence over the country's interest rates were limited because of the banking system's comfortable liquidity cushion. She said adjusting reserve requirements was one of the few effective policy tools available to the bank.
"We may even increase reserve requirements this year," she said without giving further details. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
